en: a statement or description that makes something seem larger, better, worse or more important than it really is; the act of making a statement like this
ex: a slight/gross/wild exaggeration
有点／明显的／过于夸张

zh: 提拔，提升（有时指不该得到的职位）
en: to make somebody rise to a higher rank or position, sometimes to one that they do not deserve
ex: His son was exalted to a high position in the government through family connections.
他的儿子因家庭关系而被提升为政府中的高级职位。

en: a feeling of very great joy or happiness
ex: a moment of extreme joy and exaltation
充满欢乐和高尚的时刻

zh: 地位高的；高贵的；显赫的
en: of high rank, position or great importance
ex: She was the only woman to rise to such an exalted position.
她是唯一升到如此显赫位置的女人。

zh: （对身体特定部位进行的）检查；体检
en: a formal written, spoken or practical test, especially at school or college, to see how much you know about a subject, or what you can do
ex: to take an exam
参加考试

en: a formal written, spoken or practical test, especially at school or college, to see how much you know about a subject, or what you can do
ex: successful candidates in GCSE examinations
通过普通中等教育证书考试的考生

en: to consider or study an idea, a subject, etc. very carefully
ex: This study sets out to examine in detail the possible effects of climate change.
这项研究着手详细研究气候变化的可能影响。

en: a person who is being tested to see how much they know about a subject or what they can do; a person who is taking an exam
a person who writes the questions for, or marks, a test of knowledge or ability
ex: The papers are sent to external examiners (= ones not connected with the students' school or college).
试卷送到校外主考人那里。

en: something such as an object, a fact or a situation that shows, explains or supports what you say
ex: Let me give you an example.
让我来举一个例子吧。

en: to annoy somebody very much
ex: Her moods exasperated him.
她的坏脾气让他很生气。

en: extremely annoyed, especially if you cannot do anything to improve the situation
ex: ‘Why won't you answer me?’ he asked in an exasperated voice.
“你为什么不愿意回答我？” 他愤怒地问道。

en: in an extremely annoyed way, especially because you cannot do anything to improve a situation

zh: 使人恼怒的；惹人生气的
en: extremely annoying
ex: He’s the most difficult and exasperating man I know.
他是我认识的最困难和最令人生气的人。

en: the feeling of being extremely annoyed, especially because you cannot do anything to improve a situation
ex: a groan/look/sigh of exasperation
恼怒的哼声／样子／叹息声

zh: 发掘，挖出（古建筑或古物）
挖掘，开凿，挖空（洞、隧道等）
en: to dig in the ground to look for old buildings or objects that have been buried for a long time; to find something by digging in this way
ex: The site has been excavated by archaeologists.
这个遗址已被考古学家发掘出来。

zh: （对古建筑或古物的）发掘，挖掘
en: the activity of digging in the ground to look for old buildings or objects that have been buried for a long time
ex: Further archaeological excavations are now being carried out.
更进一步的考古发掘正在进行。

en: a large machine that is used for digging and moving earth

zh: 超越（法律、命令等）的限制
en: to be greater than a particular number or amount
ex: The price will not exceed £100.
价格不会超过 100 英镑。

en: extremely; very; very much
to be very good at doing something
ex: She has always excelled in foreign languages.
她的外语从来都是出类拔萃。

en: the quality of being extremely good
ex: a reputation for academic excellence
因学术上的杰出成就而获得的声誉

zh: （用以表示愉快或赞同）好极了，妙极了
en: extremely good
ex: an excellent book/article
一本好书/文章

en: extremely well; to a very high degree
ex: The story is excellently written.
这个故事写得很好。

zh: （用于所言不包括的人或事物前）除…之外
en: used before you mention the only thing or person about which a statement is not true
ex: We work every day except Sunday.
我们除星期天外每天都工作。

en: except for; apart from
ex: The sanctions ban the sale of any products excepting medical supplies and food.
国际制裁禁止销售医药用品和食物以外的任何产品。

zh: 一般情况以外的人（或事物）；例外
规则的例外；例外的事物
en: a person or thing that is not included in a general statement
ex: Most of the buildings in the town are modern, but the church is an exception.
城里大多是现代建筑，不过教堂是个例外。

en: unusually good
ex: At the age of five he showed exceptional talent as a musician.
他五岁时就表现出非凡的音乐才能。

zh: （用于形容词和副词之前表示强调）罕见，特别，非常
只有在特殊情况下；例外地
en: used before an adjective or adverb to emphasize how strong or unusual the quality is
ex: The weather, even for January, was exceptionally cold.
这种天气即使在一月份也算得上非常寒冷。

zh: 摘录；节选；（音乐、电影的）片段
en: to take a short piece of writing, music, film, etc. from a longer whole
ex: The document was excerpted from an unidentified FBI file.
此文件摘自来源不明的联邦调查局档案。

zh: the fact of doing too much of something, especially eating or drinking
en: more than is necessary, reasonable or acceptable
ex: You can throw away any excess.
凡多余的你都可以扔掉。

en: bags, cases, etc. taken on to a plane that weigh more than the amount each passenger is allowed to carry without paying extra
ex: If your luggage exceeds 23 kg you will have to pay for excess baggage.
如果您的行李超过23公斤，则必须支付超重行李费。

en: greater than what seems reasonable or appropriate
ex: They complained about the excessive noise coming from the upstairs flat.
他们抱怨楼上发出的噪音太大。

en: to a much greater level or degree than seems reasonable or appropriate
ex: excessively high prices
过高的价格

zh: （不同国家人或团体之间的）交流，互访
en: an act of giving something to somebody or doing something for somebody and receiving something in return
ex: The exchange of prisoners took place this morning.
今天早上交换了俘虏。

zh: a former British magazine that consisted entirely of advertisements, mostly put in by individual people or small businesses. It was published every week and was started in 1868. In 2009 the magazine stopped being published, and now the advertisements, mainly for cars and other vehicles, only appear on the Exchange and Mart website.
en: a former British magazine that consisted entirely of advertisements, mostly put in by individual people or small businesses. It was published every week and was started in 1868. In 2009 the magazine stopped being published, and now the advertisements, mainly for cars and other vehicles, only appear on the Exchange and Mart website.

zh: 可交换的；可交易的；可兑换的；可更换的
en: that can be exchanged
ex: The vouchers are exchangeable for goods at selected stores.
优惠券可在指定商店兑换。

en: the government department that controlled public money. This department is now called the Treasury.
ex: This resulted in a considerable loss to the exchequer.
这使国库遭受了重大损失。

en: a government tax on some goods made, sold or used within a country
ex: new excise duties on low-alcohol drinks
低酒精饮料新的消费税

en: the act of removing something completely from something; the thing removed
ex: to demonstrate three types of surgical excision
演示三种手术切除

zh: the fact of becoming excited easily
en: the fact of becoming excited easily
ex: His excitability is infectious.
他的兴奋性很强。

en: likely to become easily excited
ex: She had trouble controlling the class of excitable ten-year-olds.
她很难管束班里这些易兴奋的十岁儿童。

en: to make somebody feel very pleased, interested or enthusiastic, especially about something that is going to happen
ex: The prospect of a year in India greatly excited her.
有望在印度待上一年使她激动万分。

en: feeling or showing happiness and enthusiasm
ex: Staff got excited when they heard they were getting a bonus.
员工听到他们正在获得奖金时感到很兴奋。

zh: in a happy and enthusiastic way
en: in a happy and enthusiastic way
ex: She waved excitedly as the car approached.
汽车开近时她激动地挥着手。

en: the state of feeling or showing happiness and enthusiasm
ex: The news caused great excitement among her friends.
这消息使她的朋友们兴奋不已。

zh: 令人激动的；使人兴奋的
en: causing great interest or excitement
ex: This is an exciting opportunity for me.
对我来说，这是一个令人兴奋的机会。

zh: 令人激动的；使人兴奋的
en: in a way that causes great interest or excitement
ex: an excitingly fast game
令人兴奋的快速游戏

zh: （尤因强烈的情感或痛苦而）惊叫，呼喊
en: to say something suddenly and loudly, especially because of strong emotion or pain
ex: She opened her eyes and exclaimed in delight at the scene.
看到这情景，她瞪着眼睛，高兴得大叫起来。

en: a short sound, word or phrase spoken suddenly to express an emotion. Oh!, Look out! and Ow! are exclamations.
ex: He gave an exclamation of surprise.
他发出一声惊叹。

en: the mark (!) that is written after an exclamation
expressing surprise or strong feelings

zh: 不包括；不放在考虑之列
防止…进入；阻止…参加；把…排斥在外
排除（…的可能性）；认为…不可能
en: to deliberately not include something in what you are doing or considering
ex: The cost of borrowing has been excluded from the inflation figures.
通胀数字未包括借贷费用。

en: not including
ex: Lunch costs £20 per person, excluding drinks.
午餐每人 10 英镑，酒水除外。

zh: 不包括在内的人（或事物）；被排除在外的人（或事物）
en: the act of preventing somebody/something from entering a place or taking part in something
ex: He was disappointed with his exclusion from the England squad.
他对自己没有入选英格兰队感到失望。

en: an official order not to go to a particular place
ex: The judge placed an exclusion order on him, banning him from city centre shops.
法官给他下了禁令，禁止他进入市中心的店铺。

en: an area where people are not allowed to enter because it is dangerous or is used for secret activities
ex: Armed forces have set up an exclusion zone around the island.
武装部队在该岛周围建立了禁区。

en: designed to prevent a particular person or group of people from taking part in something or doing something

zh: （个人或集体）专用的，专有的，独有的，独占的
排外的；不愿接收（较低社会阶层）新成员的
en: only to be used by one particular person or group; only given to one particular person or group
ex: The hotel has exclusive access to the beach.
这家旅馆有通向海滩的专用通道。

zh: for only one particular person, group or use
completely; without including anybody or anything else
en: for only one particular person, group or use
ex: The resort caters almost exclusively for a high-society public.
该度假胜地几乎完全是为上流社会的公众提供的。

zh: the practice in a group or society of not allowing other people from different groups to become members or be included
en: the fact of being of a high quality and expensive and therefore not often bought or used by most people
ex: For all its exclusiveness, the island is also thoroughly West Indian and so it is easy-going.
尽管具有排他性，但该岛还是彻头彻尾的西印度群岛，因此随和。

en: the fact of being of a high quality and expensive and therefore not often bought or used by most people
ex: The resort still preserves a feeling of exclusivity.
这个度假胜地仍然保持着特有的情调。

en: to punish somebody by officially stating that they can no longer be a member of a Christian Church, especially the Roman Catholic Church
the act of punishing somebody by officially stating that they can no longer be a member of a Christian Church, especially the Roman Catholic Church
ex: They were threatened with excommunication.
他们受到取消教籍的威胁。

en: to make a person’s skin painful, and often red, so that it starts to come off

zh: a medical condition in which a person's skin becomes painful, and often red, and so starts to come off; an area of skin that is affected by this condition
en: a medical condition in which a person's skin becomes painful, and often red, and so starts to come off; an area of skin that is affected by this condition
solid waste matter that is passed from the body through the bowels

未经处理的人体排泄物对饮用水的污染

en: relating to excrement
an ugly part that has grown on a part of an animal’s body or on a plant, caused by disease or abnormality
ex: A hard, bony excrescence was visible above one of the animal’s hooves.
在一只动物的蹄子上方可见坚硬的骨头松动。

en: solid and liquid waste matter passed from the body
ex: human excreta
人体排泄物

en: to pass solid or liquid waste matter from the body
the act of passing solid or liquid waste matter from the body; the solid or liquid waste matter that is passed in this way
ex: the excretion of toxic substances through the skin
通过皮肤排泄有毒物质

en: connected with getting rid of waste matter from the body
ex: the excretory organs
排泄器官

zh: 极痛苦的；极坏的；糟糕透顶的
en: extremely painful or bad
ex: The pain in my back was excruciating.
我的背疼痛难忍。

zh: 极痛苦的；极坏的；糟糕透顶的
en: in an extremely bad or painful way
ex: excruciatingly uncomfortable
极不舒服

zh: 证明（或宣布）无罪；为（某人）开脱
en: to prove or state officially that somebody is not guilty of something
ex: The defendant was able to exculpate himself from liability.
被告能够免除自己的责任。

zh: 证明（或宣布）无罪；为（某人）开脱
en: the act of proving or stating officially that somebody is not guilty of something
a short journey made for pleasure, especially one that has been organized for a group of people
ex: They've gone on an excursion to York.
他们到约克旅游去了。

en: that can be excused
ex: Doing it once was just about excusable—doing it twice was certainly not.
这种事干一次还可以原谅，干两次就绝对不能了。

zh: 假条（家长或医生写明请假或给假理由）
en: a reason, either true or invented, that you give to explain or defend your behaviour
ex: Late again! What's your excuse this time?
又迟到了！你这次有什么借口？

zh: （寄宿学校等机构的）短期外出许可，短假许可
en: permission from an institution such as a boarding school to be away from it for a period of time
an executive in a business

首席执行官的作用是增强团队能力。

en: very bad

高尚的诗歌

en: that can be run by a computer

zh: 成功地完成（技巧或动作）

他因叛国罪被处死。

zh: 表演；（乐曲的）演奏；（艺术品的）制作
en: the act of killing somebody, especially as a legal punishment

他因谋杀罪要以绞刑处死。

en: a person whose job or role is to kill people as a punishment, especially a public official who executes criminals

zh: （公司或机构的）经理，主管领导，管理人员
（统称公司或机构的）行政领导，领导层
en: a person who has an important job as a manager of a company or an organization
ex: company/corporate/business/industry executives
公司/企业/商业/行业主管

zh: the most senior person in an organization or department with responsibility for making daily business decisions (often used to refer to somebody who has these responsibilities in a non-profit organization)
en: the most senior person in an organization or department with responsibility for making daily business decisions (often used to refer to somebody who has these responsibilities in a non-profit organization)
ex: Linda Sarsour, the executive director, said her group helps new immigrants adjust to life in the US.
执行董事琳达·萨苏尔（Linda Sarsour）说，她的团队帮助新移民适应美国的生活。

zh: an official order from the president that becomes the law
en: an official order from the president that becomes the law

昨天，总统发布了一项行政命令，以更改国家的移民法。

zh: 行政特权，总统特权（美国总统和政府行政部门对官方文件保密的特权）
en: (in the US) the right of the president and the executive part of the government to keep official documents secret

zh: a secretary who manages the business activities of an executive or an organization
en: a secretary who manages the business activities of an executive or an organization
ex: He was executive secretary of the NAACP.
他曾是NAACP的执行秘书。

zh: a person who produces something or causes it to come into use

ex: She appointed him executor of her will.
她任命他为遗嘱执行人。

zh: （尤指宗教著作的）诠释；解经；释经

ex: biblical exegesis
圣经释经

en: a person or thing that is a good or typical example of something
ex: Her career was an exemplar of individual success at a time of great economic hardship.
在经济困难时期，她的职业生涯是个人成功的典范。

zh: 典范的；可作榜样的；可作楷模的
严厉的；儆戒性的；惩戒性的
en: providing a good example for people to copy
ex: Her behaviour was exemplary.
她的行为堪作楷模。

en: something that is a typical example of something
to be a typical example of something
ex: Her early work is exemplified in her book, ‘A Study of Children's Minds’.
她的《儿童思维研究》一书是她早期的代表作。

zh: 免除（责任、付款等）；获豁免
en: if somebody/something is exempt from something, they are not affected by it, do not have to do it, pay it, etc.

这笔钱的利息免税。

en: official permission not to do something or pay something that you would normally have to do or pay
ex: She was given exemption from the final examination.
她已获准期末免试。

（保持健康或培养技能的）一套动作，训练活动，练习

游泳是有益的运动。

en: a large ball that you can sit on when doing exercises to make your muscles work in a different way
ex: Sit upright on the exercise ball with your feet flat on the floor.
直立坐在健身球上，双脚平放在地板上。

en: a bicycle that does not move forward but is used for getting exercise indoors
a small book for students to write their work in
to use power or influence to affect somebody/something
ex: He exerted all his authority to make them accept the plan.
他利用他的所有权力让他们接受这个计划。

en: physical or mental effort; the act of making an effort
ex: She was hot and breathless from the exertion of cycling uphill.
她骑车上山累得全身发热，喘不过气来。

zh: （剧本中的说明，两个或以上演员）退场，下场
en: used in a play as a written instruction that tells two or more actors to leave the stage
ex: Exeunt Antony and Cleopatra.
安东尼和克娄巴特拉退场。

en: to remove dead cells from the surface of skin in order to make it smoother
the act of removing dead cells from the surface of skin in order to make it smoother
ex: Regular deep-cleansing and exfoliation should be part of your beauty routine.
定期的深层清洁和去角质应成为您日常美容的一部分。

zh: 呼出，吐出（肺中的空气、烟等）；呼气
en: an act of breathing out the air or smoke that is in your lungs; an amount of air or smoke that you breathe out
ex: Carbon dioxide is eliminated from the body during exhalation.
呼气期间会从体内清除二氧化碳。

zh: 呼出，吐出（肺中的空气、烟等）；呼气
en: to breathe out the air or smoke, etc. in your lungs
ex: He sat back and exhaled deeply.
他仰坐着深深地呼气。

zh: （车辆、发动机或机器排出的）废气

ex: car exhaust fumes/emissions
汽车排出的废气；汽车排放物

en: a pipe through which waste gases come out of a vehicle
ex: The car's exhaust pipe was blocked with snow.
汽车的排气管被雪堵住了。

zh: 筋疲力尽的；疲惫不堪的
en: very tired
ex: I'm exhausted!
我累死了！

zh: 使人疲惫不堪的；令人筋疲力尽的
en: making you feel very tired
ex: an exhausting day at work
工作得筋疲力尽的一天

en: the state of being very tired
ex: suffering from physical/mental/nervous exhaustion
身体／精神／神经衰弱

en: including everything possible; very careful or complete
ex: exhaustive research/tests
彻底的研究；全面的测试

zh: in a very careful or complete way
en: in a very careful or complete way
ex: Every product is exhaustively tested before being sold.
每件产品销售前都经过全面检验。

zh: 表现，显示，显出（感情、品质或能力）
en: to show something in a public place for people to enjoy or to give them information
ex: They will be exhibiting their new designs at the trade fairs.
他们将在商品交易会上展出他们新的设计。

zh: （技能、感情或行为的）表现，显示，表演
en: a collection of things, for example works of art, that are shown to the public
ex: Have you seen the Picasso exhibition?
你看过毕加索的画展吗？

en: behaviour that is intended to make people notice or admire you

zh: a person suffering from a mental condition that makes them want to show their sexual organs in public
en: a person who likes to make other people notice him or her
ex: Children are natural exhibitionists.
儿童天生好表现自己。

en: a person or a company that shows their work or products to the public
ex: The work of over 500 exhibitors will be on display at the arts and crafts show.
超过500家参展商的作品将在工艺品展览中展出。

en: to make somebody feel very happy and excited
ex: Speed had always exhilarated him.
速度总让他感到兴奋。

en: very happy and excited
ex: I felt exhilarated after a morning of skiing.
我滑了一上午的雪兴奋不已。

zh: 使人兴奋的；令人激动的；令人高兴的
en: very exciting and great fun
ex: My first parachute jump was an exhilarating experience.
我第一次跳伞的经历很令人激动。

en: a feeling of being very happy and excited
ex: the exhilaration of performing on stage
在舞台上演出的激动心情

en: to try hard to persuade somebody to do something
ex: The party leader exhorted his members to start preparing for government.
该党领袖敦促党员着手准备筹建政府的工作。

en: an act of trying very hard to persuade somebody to do something
ex: The play becomes a strong exhortation to enjoy life while you still can.
该剧成为人们尽力享受生活的强烈劝告。

en: an act of removing a dead body from the ground, especially in order to examine how the person died
ex: A committee was appointed to supervise the exhumation and identification of the bodies.
任命了一个委员会来监督尸体的尸体挖掘和鉴定。

en: to remove a dead body from the ground especially in order to examine how the person died
ex: The body was exhumed on the order of the judge.
尸体是在法官的命令下发掘的。

en: a need or demand that you must deal with immediately

战争的应急措施

en: very small in size or amount; hardly enough
ex: an exiguous salary
高薪

zh: 流亡国外者；被流放者；离乡背井者
en: the state of being sent to live in another country that is not your own, especially for political reasons or as a punishment
ex: a place of exile
流放地

zh: （尤指在困境或贫困中）生活，生存
en: to be real; to be present in a place or situation
ex: Does life exist on other planets?
其他行星上有生命吗？

zh: （尤指艰难或无聊的）生活，生活方式
en: the state or fact of being real or living or of being present
ex: I was unaware of his existence until today.
直到今天我才知道有他这么个人。

en: existing; real
ex: creatures existent in nature
自然界中现存的生物

zh: 关于人类存在的；与人类存在有关的
en: connected with human existence
the theory that humans are free and responsible for their own actions in a world without meaning
a person who believes in the theory that humans are free and responsible for their own actions in a world without meaning
ex: Sartre was an existentialist.
萨特是个存在主义者。

en: found or used now
ex: New laws will soon replace existing legislation.
新法即将取代现行法规。

zh: （车辆可以从一道路驶出进入另一道路的）出口，出路
退出；离去；（尤指演员）退场
en: a way out of a public building or vehicle
ex: Where's the exit?
出口在哪儿？

en: an exam that you take at the end of the last year in school or at the end of a period of training
ex: a high school exit exam
中学毕业考试
